sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajendra Kumar Srivastava,Vinay Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikram D. Chauhan,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant application has been preferred with the prayer to release the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.85 of 2020, under Sections 323, 307, 498A, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Shikohabad, District Firozabad.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is the husband of the victim and as per the allegations in the first information report it is alleged that the applicant along with the family members have demanded the dowry and thereafter, have assaulted the victim.

Thereafter,
the applicant and his family members have poured kerosene oil, as a result of the same, the victim has suffered 40-50% burn injuries.
As per the medical report, the injuries are thermal burn injuries sustained by hot liquid.
The victim has given her statement,which is at page 27 of the paper book in which she has made allegations against the applicant with regard to pouring of hot oil.

Raju vs State Of U.P. on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21799783/
1
On a pointed query being made to the learned counsel for the applicant as to how the victim has suffered burn injuries, learned counsel for the applicant could not given any explanation.
The burn injuries along with the statement of the victim are indicative of the fact that the victim has been harassed by the applicant and his family members.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, the bail application lacks merit and is accordingly, dismissed.
